checks.title: Descriptor canonical form matches user input
Script type matches declared wallet type
Master fingerprint present for every key
Derivation path present for every key
Multisig threshold and key count extracted
Receive and change derive same script type
Receive and change differ only in chain index
First N receive addresses derive without error
First N change addresses derive without error
Known address matches a derived address

critical_issues.title: User's known address does not match any address in the derived range
critical_issues.description: Descriptor is wrong, or address belongs to another wallet

warnings.title: Change descriptor missing
warnings.description: A complete recovery backup should include both receive and change descriptors. Without the change descriptor, an empty wallet restore will not see funds returned to change addresses.
warnings.recommended_fix: Export both descriptors from your wallet software. In Sparrow: File > Export Wallet > Output Descriptor. In Bitcoin Core: listdescriptors true.

warnings.title: No wallet birth height documented
warnings.description: Without a creation date or block height, a recovery wallet must scan the whole chain, which is slow and can miss funds if the gap limit is exceeded.
warnings.recommended_fix: Record the wallet's creation date or the block height at first use alongside your descriptor backup.

warnings.title: Gap limit not documented
warnings.description: If you have used many addresses, a default gap limit (20) may stop a recovery wallet before it finds all your funds.
warnings.recommended_fix: Note the highest address index you have used, or your wallet's configured gap limit, with your backup.

warnings.title: No printed descriptor backup
warnings.description: A descriptor stored only on a computer can be lost with the device. A printed or stamped copy survives disk failure and software changes.
warnings.recommended_fix: Print at least two copies of the descriptor backup and store them in separate, secure locations.

warnings.title: No recovery drill in the last 12 months
warnings.description: A recovery plan that has never been rehearsed end-to-end is untested. Hardware, software, and memory all change over time.
warnings.recommended_fix: Run a Disaster Drill in Lifeboat v0.3 when available, or rehearse a recovery on a test network now.

warnings.title: No heir instructions written
warnings.description: Without written instructions, the people you intend to inherit your bitcoin may not know the materials exist or how to use them.
warnings.recommended_fix: Write a plain-language recovery runbook for your heirs and store it with your estate documents.

warnings.title: No emergency contact named
warnings.description: No trusted person is recorded to help an heir who gets stuck during recovery.
warnings.recommended_fix: Name a trusted, Bitcoin-literate contact in your recovery instructions.

warnings.title: Hardware wallet not exercised recently
warnings.description: A hardware signer that has not signed anything in over a year may have a dead battery, corrupted firmware, or a forgotten PIN.
warnings.recommended_fix: Sign a test transaction on a test network with each hardware device.

warnings.title: Wallet software not documented
warnings.description: If you do not record which wallet software your setup depends on, an heir may not know how to load the descriptor.
warnings.recommended_fix: Note the wallet software (and version) needed to use this descriptor, and prefer descriptor-based recovery that works in multiple wallets.

next_steps.action: Confirm the descriptor belongs to this wallet; the known address did not match the derived range.
Write down your wallet's creation date or block height.
Print two copies of the descriptor backup.
Run a Disaster Drill in Lifeboat v0.3 when available.
Write recovery instructions for your heirs.
Sign a test transaction with each hardware device.
Document which wallet software your setup needs.

anti_actions: Do not store the descriptor in cloud notes apps.
Do not photograph this report and send it on chat.

disclaimer_long:
About this document

Bitcoin Lifeboat is an open-source diagnostic and rehearsal tool.
This document reflects only the information you provided. It cannot
detect missing materials Lifeboat was not asked to check, it cannot
verify the physical location or condition of your backups, and it
cannot predict the future condition of your hardware wallets.

A "Ready" status means the metadata you provided appears complete
for the scenarios Lifeboat tested. It does not mean your bitcoin
is safe. It does not mean recovery will succeed in a real emergency.

You are responsible for verifying recovery end-to-end on a test
network before trusting your real wallet. Consult an attorney for
estate planning. Consult a tax professional for tax implications.

Bitcoin Lifeboat does not custody funds, does not contact you,
does not call you, and does not ask for your seed phrase.

If anyone claiming to be from Bitcoin Lifeboat contacts you, it
is a scam. Hang up.
